title: Identification of markers that distinguish adipose tissue and glucose and insulin metabolism using a multi-modal machine learning approach
summary: Multimodal XGBoost ranked serum metabolites against measured glucose, insulin, adipose and ectopic-fat phenotypes in 53 men; the study reports specific associations, with small-cohort limits. Clinical, biochemical, MRI and metabolomic measures are the reference endpoints; result is an association/feature-importance analysis without external cohort validation.
ai_technology: multimodal extreme-gradient-boosting models rank predictors for glucose/insulin measures, adipose morphology and fat distribution.
organization: The Lundberg Laboratory for Diabetes Research; The Sahlgrenska Academy at the University of Gothenburg; Institute of Medicine; University of Gothenburg

evidence.tested: Results associate named metabolites with fasting glucose/insulin, OGTT and adipocyte/ectopic-fat outcomes; 53 non-obese male participants.
evidence.unknown: Clinical, biochemical, MRI and metabolomic measures are the reference endpoints; result is an association/feature-importance analysis without external cohort validation. The source does not establish benefits beyond the reported evaluation.
evidence.ai_role: multimodal extreme-gradient-boosting models rank predictors for glucose/insulin measures, adipose morphology and fat distribution.

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
